content.title: Phase 9 — Overflow handling
content.subtitle: When content is too big, the compiler splits the slide

body.heading: Each layout declares what it supports
bullets: Hard filter: an intent that needs 'chart' will not pick a layout whose supports excludes it
Inferred from intent's slot strategies via STRATEGY_TO_KIND
Layouts not in the registry default to permissive — unknown templates still work
Run `--list-capabilities` to print every layout's supported kinds

content.title: The compiler now estimates content density

body.heading: How splitting decisions are made
bullets: Each instruction is evaluated against the geometry of its target slot
Bullets: lines required vs lines that fit (width × char density)
Tables: rows × columns vs slot capacity at OW row/column heights
Variadic content (KPI dashboards): item count vs available slots
Splitting target: ≈ 0.9 density per page; >1.0 triggers a split
Other instructions on the slide are repeated unchanged across pages

content.title: Long bullet list — the compiler should split this

body.heading: Eighteen bullets that should not fit on one slide
bullets: First bullet — describes a step in the workflow that involves several distinct sub-tasks the team must coordinate across regions and product lines
Second bullet — covers data ingestion from upstream systems and how schema drift is detected before processing reaches the warehouse
Third bullet — explains the validation pipeline that runs every night to catch anomalies in the pricing feed and inventory snapshots
Fourth bullet — walks through the model retraining cadence and the criteria for promoting a candidate model to production traffic
Fifth bullet — describes governance and approval workflow with named owners for every stage and clearly written exit criteria
Sixth bullet — covers the observability stack and the SLOs we hold ourselves to during peak hours and major release windows
Seventh bullet — addresses change management when a new contract is signed mid-quarter and how scope is rebalanced across teams
Eighth bullet — outlines the escalation path when a critical regression is detected post-deploy and the rollback decision tree
Ninth bullet — talks about how feedback from sales engineers is incorporated into the next iteration through the council process
Tenth bullet — discusses the measurement approach we use to quantify the impact of each release on revenue and retention
Eleventh bullet — describes the dependency we have on the upstream identity service and its SLAs for authentication latency
Twelfth bullet — summarises the open risks for the next planning cycle and the proposed mitigations for each high-severity item
Thirteenth bullet — explains how we balance technical debt paydown against new feature work in the quarterly roadmap
Fourteenth bullet — covers the incident review cadence and the blameless postmortem template we use to capture learnings
Fifteenth bullet — describes the runbook automation we built last quarter and the metrics tracking adoption across teams
Sixteenth bullet — explains the experimentation framework and how A/B variants are gated behind feature flags before rollout
Seventeenth bullet — covers the customer success motion that reduces churn during the first ninety days of a new account
Eighteenth bullet — closes with the open questions we will tackle in the strategy offsite next month and the expected outputs

insight.title: Density
insight.text: Charts don't trigger density splits; they scale to the slot.

body.heading: What changed
bullets: Layout capability registry hard-filters incompatible (intent, layout) pairs
Density evaluator estimates fit per slot for bullets and tables
Variadic overflow (dashboard) splits the metric list across multiple plans
Density overflow (bullets, tables) splits the offending payload
compile_slide() now returns List[CompilationPlan]; the executor loops
